key_insight: Reinforcement learning and Bayesian optimisation can find strong upper bounds for hard-to-compute link invariants, enabling many new exact values when combined with lower bounds.
engineering_relevance: This shows machine learning can guide search in discrete mathematical spaces where exact algorithms are unavailable, suggesting a general strategy for hard optimization problems in computational science.
method: Train reinforcement-learning agents to search for unlinking/slicing trajectories.
Use Bayesian optimisation to propose candidate moves and improve upper bounds.
Combine learned upper bounds with known lower bounds to certify exact invariant values where possible.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports new upper bounds, new exact values in many cases, and reproduction of known non-additivity counterexamples, including some new unknotting trajectories.
watch_item: The approach depends on heuristic search and auxiliary lower bounds, so results are not guaranteed to be exhaustive or definitive when the bounds do not meet exactly.
paper_title: Computations of the slice genus and the unknotting number of links via machine learning
